text: Fowl Pox is a relatively slow-spreading viral disease, transmitted by contact or mosquito bite, that can persist in a flock for several months. Dry pox starts as small whitish spots developing into wart-like nodules on featherless areas (comb, wattles, ear lobes, eyes, sometimes feet). Wet pox affects the mouth and upper respiratory tract (especially larynx and trachea), showing as plaques there. Fowl Pox causes depression, reduced appetite, and poor growth or egg production, with significant mortality in young chicks; an individual bird's illness runs 3–5 weeks. Treatment: none. Prevention: vaccination via the wing web method, usable in chicks as young as 1 day old; check for a 'take' (skin swelling or scab at the vaccination site) 7–10 days after vaccination to confirm it worked.
